items.title: Hackers Exploited the PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
items.summary: Amazon Web Services logged attempts to leverage the internet-melting PHP2Shell bugs four days ago. They’re now being “broadly exploited” across the internet.
items.author: Lily Hay Newman

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
items.summary: Meta’s board feared that its CEO’s departure could disrupt the company’s AI ambitions. A new stock agreement gives him financial incentives to stay put.
items.author: Paresh Dave

items.title: This Startup Is All In on Recursive Self-Improvement. Its Latest Model Is Scary Good
items.summary: Recursive makes the case that the benefits of using AI to build AI outweigh the risks.
items.author: Will Knight

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Vision for Europe Runs on Plug-In Data Centers
items.summary: At Nvidia’s GTC in Berlin, Huang unveiled the company’s new plug-in data center—the DSX Pod—as the key to unlocking Europe’s AI infrastructure lag. Oh, and autonomous humanoid robotics.
items.author: Tom Bristow

items.title: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
items.summary: The PHP Foundation has revealed two serious vulnerabilities that could impact millions of websites. Security experts warn that failure to quickly patch the flaws could have dire consequences.
items.author: Matt Burgess, Lily Hay Newman

items.title: AI Guardrails Aren’t Stopping Criminal Hackers
items.summary: Hackers around the world are all-in on using agentic AI to wage attacks—and manipulating tools like Anthropic’s Claude to help them carry out their crimes.
items.author: Lily Hay Newman

items.title: A Design Flaw in Share Links Exposes Users’ Personal Conversations With Meta’s Muse
items.summary: The company is suspending the feature after security researchers discovered how easy it was to access sensitive information shared with the AI assistant.
items.author: Dan Goodin, Ars Technica

items.title: OpenAI Invests in Startup That Uses Brain Implants to Detect Cancer
items.summary: It’s the latest in a growing wave of bets that AI companies are making on brain data.
items.author: Emily Mullin

items.title: Europe Wants Data Centers. Its Climate Goals Are Getting in the Way
items.summary: A plan to funnel the heat given off by data centers into nearby homes has run aground in Germany. Across Europe, policymakers are weighing AI ambitions against climate objectives.
items.author: Joel Khalili
